problems.title: I can't see my object
problems.summary: Object invisible, vanished or lost from view.

causes.text: The scene is empty, so there is nothing to see yet.
The active object is hidden. Reveal hidden objects.
You may be zoomed too far in or out. Show everything in the scene.
Select the object (click its name in the Outliner at the top-right), then zoom to it.
In the Outliner, a closed eye icon means the object is hidden. Click the eye to show it.
Keep the mouse pointer over the 3D viewport. Shortcuts act on whichever area the pointer is over.
You are not in Object Mode. Many shortcuts behave differently in other modes.
Nothing is selected. Click an object first.
If a text box is active, press Esc first, then move the pointer back to the viewport.
Number keys on the top row and the numpad do different things. No numpad? Turn on Emulate Numpad in Edit > Preferences > Input.

problems.title: I'm stuck in another mode
problems.summary: Stuck in Edit, Sculpt or another mode.

causes.text: You are not in Object Mode. Press Tab, or use the mode menu at the top-left of the viewport.
If you are in Object Mode already, you are fine. Press Tab with a mesh selected when you want to edit its shape.
Make sure the Select Box tool is active at the top of the left toolbar.
You are in another mode. In Edit Mode you select parts of one object, not other objects.
The object may be locked from selection. In the Outliner, open the Filter menu, turn on the selectability arrow, then click the arrow beside the object.
Try selecting everything with A, or clear the selection with Alt + A, then click again.

problems.title: Everything looks like wireframe or see-through
problems.summary: Viewport shows lines only or looks transparent.

causes.text: The viewport is in Wireframe shading.
Use the four shading buttons at the top-right of the viewport: Wireframe, Solid, Material Preview, Rendered. Solid is the normal working view.
If the object looks see-through in Solid view, X-Ray may be on. Press Alt + Z to toggle it.

problems.title: Faces look dark, black or inside-out
problems.summary: Shading looks wrong or surfaces are inverted.

causes.text: Faces may be pointing the wrong way. In Edit Mode, select everything (A), then use Mesh > Normals > Recalculate Outside (Shift + N).
To check, open the Overlays dropdown in the viewport header and turn on Face Orientation. Blue is correct, red is flipped.
In Material Preview without a light, things can look dark. Try Solid view.

problems.title: I did something by accident
problems.summary: Moved, deleted or changed something by mistake.

causes.text: Undo it with Ctrl + Z. Press it again to go back further.
To jump back several steps at once, use Edit > Undo History.

problems.title: No middle mouse button or numpad
problems.summary: Laptop or trackpad without the keys Blender expects.

causes.text: Turn on Emulate 3 Button Mouse in Edit > Preferences > Input. Then Alt + left-drag orbits the view.
Turn on Emulate Numpad in the same place to use the top number row as a numpad.
You can also drag the small axis gizmo at the top-right of the viewport to orbit, and use the View menu for standard views.

problems.title: My object looks blocky or rough
problems.summary: Surfaces look faceted instead of smooth.

causes.text: With the object selected, open the Object menu (or right-click in the viewport) and choose Shade Smooth.
For a rounder shape, add a Subdivision Surface modifier with Ctrl + 1 in Object Mode.

problems.title: My object is tiny, huge or off-centre

causes.text: Press N in the viewport and open the Item tab to see Location, Rotation, Scale and Dimensions.
To reset in Object Mode: Alt + G clears location, Alt + R clears rotation, Alt + S clears scale.
Think the object is far away? Show everything in the scene.

problems.title: A panel, toolbar or tab disappeared
problems.summary: Parts of the Blender screen are missing.

causes.text: With the pointer over the viewport, press N to show or hide the right sidebar and T to show or hide the left toolbar.
Ctrl + Space maximises the area under the pointer. Press it again to restore the layout.
Check the workspace tabs at the top (Layout, Modeling, Sculpting). Click Layout for the default arrangement.
The Properties editor (Modifiers and Material tabs) is on the right. Its tabs only appear when an object is selected.

problems.title: Blender is slow or laggy
problems.summary: Viewport is slow, choppy or freezing.

causes.text: Rendered view is heavy. Switch to Solid.
Material Preview is slower than Solid. Use Solid while modelling.
High modifier levels (like Subdivision Surface) slow things down. Lower the Levels Viewport number.

problems.title: I want to save or recover my work
problems.summary: Saving files and recovering after a crash.

causes.text: Save with Ctrl + S over the viewport. The first time, choose a name and folder.
After a crash, try File > Recover > Recover Last Session.
Use File > Save As with a new name before big experiments.

problems.title: Moving or scaling goes the wrong way
problems.summary: Object jumps, slides sideways or snaps to odd places.

causes.text: Snapping may be on (the magnet icon in the header is lit). Click the magnet to turn it off, or press Shift + Tab.
An axis lock may be active. While moving, press the same axis key (X, Y or Z) twice, or press the middle mouse button, to clear it.
Numbers you typed during the move count. Right click or Esc cancels the move and you can try again.
The pivot point may be set to something unusual. Check the Pivot dropdown in the header and choose Median Point.
Press Ctrl + Z to undo the odd move.

problems.title: It rotates or scales around a strange point
problems.summary: Object swings around the wrong spot.

causes.text: The object's origin dot is not in the middle. Object menu > Set Origin > Origin to Geometry.
The Pivot Point may be set to 3D Cursor. Open the Pivot dropdown in the header and pick Median Point.
The 3D cursor may be far away. Press Shift + C to bring it back to the centre.

problems.title: My modifier does nothing
problems.summary: Added Mirror, Array or another modifier and nothing changes.

causes.text: No modifier is on the active object. Select the object first, then open the wrench tab.
The modifier may be switched off. In the wrench tab, make sure the monitor and camera icons on the modifier are lit.
Settings may be zero. Array needs Count above 1 and an offset. Solidify needs a Thickness other than 0.
The object's scale may not be applied. Press Ctrl + A > Scale in Object Mode.
You may be looking at the wrong object. Click the object with the modifier and look at the wrench tab.

problems.title: Extrude, loop cut or bevel does nothing
problems.summary: A modelling tool refuses to work or does something strange.

causes.text: These tools only work in Edit Mode. Select your mesh and press Tab.
Nothing is selected. In Edit Mode select points, edges or faces first (keys 1, 2, 3 choose which).
The mouse must be over the 3D viewport, not a side panel.
Press F9 or open the small panel at the bottom-left to adjust the settings.

problems.title: My render is black or empty
problems.summary: Pressing F12 gives a dark, blank or wrong picture.

causes.text: There may be no camera. Add one with Shift + A > Camera, then press Ctrl + Alt + Numpad 0 to aim it.
The scene may have no light. Add one with Shift + A > Light > Sun.
The camera may be pointing away from your object. Press Numpad 0 to look through it and move it until you see the object.
Objects may be hidden in the render. In the Outliner check the camera icon next to the object.
